title: Finite modules descend from an element localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $f\in R$, and let $R_f$ be the localization of $R$ at $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $L$ be a finitely generated $R_f$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then there are a finitely generated $R$-module $M$ and an isomorphism of $R_f$-modules $M_f\cong L$, where $M_f$ is the localization of $M$ at the multiplicative set $\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].

source.place: Tag 05N5 (algebra-lemma-construct-fp-module), clause (1), line 31490; specialize the multiplicative set to powers of f and I=0

proof.text: Choose a finite set s of generators of L over R_f using Module.Finite.fg_top [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Restrict scalars to R and put N = span_R(s), the image in L of the finite free R-module on s. This is the quotient R^n/K in Tag 05N5(1), with K the inverse image of the kernel of R_f^n → L. Submodule.fg_span proves N is a finite R-module.

source.place: Tag 05N5, proof of clause (1), lines 31504–31508; realize R^n/K as its image N in L

proof.text: The identity of L is a localization map at S = powers(f), since L is already an R_f-module [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Apply Submodule.localized'_span to this identity map: the localization of N inside L is span_{R_f}(s), which is top by the choice of s. Submodule.isLocalizedModule identifies the map from N to this localized submodule as a localization map. Thus its abstract localization is R_f-linearly isomorphic to L, using IsLocalizedModule.mapEquiv and the equivalence from the top submodule to L.

source.place: Tag 05N5, proof of clause (1), lines 31504–31508, with the module localization construction in Section 00CM

proof.text: To obtain a model in the universe of R, use Submodule.FG.small: a finitely generated R-submodule has a small underlying type. Take M = Shrink N with the transported module structure and the proved equivalence Shrink.linearEquiv R N. Finiteness transports along this equivalence. IsLocalizedModule.mapEquiv transports its localization and gives the required R_f-linear isomorphism from M_f to L. This also covers the zero ring, f=0 or nilpotent, and an empty generating set, without further hypotheses.
